Wait, wait. Let's drill down to how narrative actually works here.

P1) The narrative is about oneself & the world
P2) The world (as I narrate it) will conclude that I am male.
P3) Test/Challenge: Given that my narrative about myself says I am a woman, how will that effect my narrative about the world?
replies.author: BSRK Aditya

Something this post (and the blog as a whole, but this post and a few others in
particular) makes me think about is, how do autogynephilia and sexual orientation relate to scrupulosity? There could be a correlation, one way or another, between AGP,
sexual orientation and seeing what to do about your gender issues as a weighty moral dilemma. For example, do AGPs give more (or less) weight to considerations about how their transition would affect cis women? How do gynephile AGPs compare to this dimension to bi, GAMP and androphile AGPs?
